specName: Semantic Gaps — Wire Memories Table, Fix Graph Population, Emit WAL Events
title: rorca-semantic-gaps
_notes: The semantic wiring spec (SW-001–012) connected pgvector + AGE to spec generation, but three gaps remain: (1) auto-memory writes to the `memories` table but never emits `memory_created` WAL events, so the embedding pipeline and graph populator never see them. (2) backfillAll() only reads MEMORY.md from filesystem — not the 139 memories in the DB `memories` table. (3) The knowledge graph has 0 vertices/0 edges because AGE cypher() calls fail silently via the connection pool (AGE requires per-session LOAD 'age' + SET search_path). Also fixes context-cache queries that read from wal_events for memory instead of the memories table.
_relatesTo: rorca-semantic-wiring (SW-001–012, just completed), rorca-postgres-migration (PG-015 AGE, PG-020–023 auto-memory)
_executionOrder: Run immediately. All infrastructure exists. No new tables needed.

userStories.title: Emit memory_created WAL Events from Auto-Memory
userStories.description:
The auto-memory system (`backend/src/lib/auto-memory.ts`) inserts memories into the `memories` table at three locations (lines ~161, ~337, ~565) but NEVER emits `memory_created` WAL events to the SSE hub. This means the embedding pipeline (`embedding-pipeline.ts:544`) and graph populator (`graph-populator.ts:52`) never learn about new memories.

After each successful `INSERT INTO memories` call in auto-memory.ts, emit a WAL event:
1. Import `broadcastAll` from `./sse-hub`.
2. After each INSERT INTO memories succeeds, call:
```typescript
broadcastAll({
  event_type: 'memory_created',
  workspace_id: workspaceId,
  spec_id: sourceSpecId || null,
  story_id: storyId || null,
  payload: JSON.stringify({ id: memoryId, text: entry.content, category: entry.category }),
});
```
3. To get the `memoryId`, change the INSERT to use `RETURNING id` and capture the returned row.
4. There are THREE insert locations in auto-memory.ts:
   - Line ~161: `synthesizeStoryMemory()` — per-story memories after story completion
   - Line ~337: `synthesizeSpecMemory()` — spec-level memories after generation
   - Line ~565: `synthesizeRunMemory()` — run-level memories after pipeline completion
   All three need the WAL event emission.
5. Also insert the WAL event into the `wal_events` table (not just broadcast) so it persists:
```typescript
await execute(
  `INSERT INTO wal_events (event_type, workspace_id, spec_id, story_id, payload) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)`,
  ['memory_created', workspaceId, sourceSpecId || null, storyId || null, JSON.stringify({ id: memoryId, text: entry.content, category: entry.category })]
);
```
acceptanceCriteria: All three INSERT INTO memories locations in auto-memory.ts emit memory_created WAL events
WAL events are both broadcast via SSE hub AND persisted to wal_events table
Each WAL event payload includes memory id, text content, and category
INSERT uses RETURNING id to capture the generated memory ID
broadcastAll is imported from ./sse-hub
Embedding pipeline receives memory_created events and enqueues embedding jobs
Graph populator receives memory_created events and creates Memory nodes
npx tsc --noEmit passes in backend/

userStories.title: Backfill Embeddings from memories Table (Not Just MEMORY.md)
userStories.description:
The `backfillAll()` function in `backend/src/lib/embedding-pipeline.ts` (line ~841) only reads memories from the filesystem `MEMORY.md` file. There are 139 memories in the `memories` database table that are never embedded.

Add a step 4b to `backfillAll()` after the existing MEMORY.md step (line ~856):
1. Query the `memories` table: `SELECT id, workspace_id, category, content FROM memories WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`.
2. Filter by workspaceId if provided.
3. For each memory row, prepare text as `prepareText('memory', row.content)`, compute hash, check staleness, and enqueue embedding job with `sourceType: 'memory'` and `sourceId: row.id`.
4. Use `source_id` format like `mem-{id}` to avoid collision with MEMORY.md entry IDs (which use line-based IDs like `entry-1`).
5. This should come AFTER the MEMORY.md step so filesystem memories take precedence in staleness checks.
acceptanceCriteria: backfillAll() queries the memories table for active (non-deleted) memories
Memory rows are prepared, hashed, staleness-checked, and enqueued for embedding
Source IDs use mem-{id} format to avoid collision with MEMORY.md entry IDs
Memories are filtered by workspaceId when provided
Running POST /api/admin/embed-all after this change embeds all 139 DB memories
GET /api/admin/embed-all/status shows increased memoryCount after backfill
npx tsc --noEmit passes in backend/

userStories.title: Fix context-cache getRecentMemory to Read from memories Table
userStories.description:
The `getRecentMemory()` function in `backend/src/lib/context-cache.ts` (line ~286) queries `wal_events` for `memory_created`/`memory_updated` events to get recent memories. But memories are stored in the `memories` table — and before SG-001, no WAL events were ever emitted. Even after SG-001, historical memories won't have WAL events.

Rewrite `getRecentMemory()` to query the `memories` table directly:
1. Replace the WAL events query with:
```typescript
const rows = await query<{ id: string; content: string; category: string; created_at: string }>(
  `SELECT id, content, category, created_at FROM memories
   WHERE workspace_id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL
   ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50`,
  [workspaceId],
);
```
2. Map rows to `{ text: row.content, ts: row.created_at }` format (same interface as before).
3. Remove the JSON.parse(payload) logic since we're reading content directly.
4. This ensures getRecentMemory() returns memories even if no WAL events exist.
acceptanceCriteria: getRecentMemory() queries the memories table directly instead of wal_events
Returns up to 50 most recent non-deleted memories ordered by created_at DESC
Output format unchanged: Array<{ text: string; ts: string }>
Works for workspaces that have memories but no memory_created WAL events
Cache behavior preserved (warm tier, 2 min TTL)
npx tsc --noEmit passes in backend/

userStories.title: Fix AGE Cypher Execution — Per-Connection Session Setup
userStories.description:
Apache AGE requires `LOAD 'age'` and `SET search_path = ag_catalog, ...` to be run on EACH database connection before any Cypher queries work. The `knowledge-graph.ts` file (line ~125) does this correctly via `withGraphClient()` which acquires a raw `pg` client, runs the setup, then executes Cypher. However, the graph has 0 vertices and 0 edges, which means either:

1. `withGraphClient()` is never called (graph populator events never fire), OR
2. The Cypher queries fail silently.

Investigate and fix:

1. In `knowledge-graph.ts`, add `logger.info` to `withGraphClient()` (line ~120) to log when a graph client is acquired and released.
2. In each `cypherMutate()` call (line ~172), add error logging with the actual Cypher query that failed.
3. Check `isGraphAvailable()` — it may be returning `false` due to a cached negative result. The check queries `ag_catalog.ag_graph` — verify this works with the connection pool (it also needs `LOAD 'age'`). If the availability check itself needs the session setup, fix it to use `withGraphClient()` instead of a bare query.
4. In `graph-populator.ts`, add `logger.info` at the top of each handler (`handleRunFinished`, `handleSpecApproved`, `handleStoryCompleted`, `handleMemoryCreated`) so we can see which events are being received.
5. Verify that `populateFromSpec()` and `populateFromRun()` in knowledge-graph.ts use `withGraphClient()` for ALL their Cypher operations (not bare `execute()` calls).
acceptanceCriteria: withGraphClient() logs when graph client is acquired and released
cypherMutate() logs failed Cypher queries with the query text
isGraphAvailable() correctly detects AGE — uses withGraphClient() if needed for the availability check
Graph populator handlers log when they receive WAL events
All Cypher operations in populateFromSpec() and populateFromRun() use withGraphClient()
After fix, approving a spec creates Story and Spec vertices in the graph
npx tsc --noEmit passes in backend/

userStories.title: Add Graph Backfill Endpoint — Populate from Existing Runs and Specs
userStories.description:
The knowledge graph has 0 vertices because the graph populator only processes WAL events going FORWARD. Existing specs (77) and runs need to be backfilled into the graph.

Create `POST /api/admin/graph-backfill` endpoint in `backend/src/routes/backups.ts`:
1. Import `populateFromSpec`, `populateFromRun`, `isGraphAvailable`, `graphStats` from `../lib/knowledge-graph`.
2. Check `isGraphAvailable()` first — return 400 if AGE is not installed.
3. Query all approved specs: `SELECT id, path FROM workspaces` then scan each workspace's `forge/specs/approved/*.json`.
4. For each spec JSON, call `populateFromSpec(specId, workspaceId, stories)` where stories are from `userStories` array.
5. Query all completed runs: `SELECT id, spec_path, workspace_id FROM pipeline_runs WHERE status IN ('done', 'passed')`. For each, call `populateFromRun(runId, specId, workspaceId)`.
6. Return `{ specsProcessed, runsProcessed, stats: graphStats() }` showing the resulting vertex/edge counts.
7. Also add `GET /api/admin/graph-stats` that just returns `graphStats()` for monitoring.
8. Add `@swagger` JSDoc annotations for both endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/graph-backfill exists and populates graph from existing specs and runs
Checks isGraphAvailable() before processing — returns 400 if AGE not installed
Processes all approved spec JSONs from all workspace filesystem paths
Processes all completed pipeline_runs via populateFromRun()
Returns specsProcessed count, runsProcessed count, and graphStats()
GET /api/admin/graph-stats returns current vertex/edge counts
Both endpoints have @swagger JSDoc annotations
After running backfill, graph has non-zero vertices and edges
npx tsc --noEmit passes in backend/

userStories.title: Fix search.ts Keyword Search to Query memories Table
userStories.description:
The `hybridSearch()` function in `backend/src/lib/search.ts` (line ~126) does keyword search against `wal_events` for memory type (`memory_created`/`memory_updated` events). Like SG-003, this misses memories that were written directly to the `memories` table without WAL events.

Update the keyword search leg for memory source type:
1. In `search.ts`, find the keyword search section that builds the SQL query (around line ~126-160).
2. For `sourceType = 'memory'`, change the query from scanning `wal_events` to scanning the `memories` table:
```sql
SELECT id::text as source_id, 'memory' as source_type,
       category as title, content as snippet,
       ts_rank_cd(tsv, query) as rank
FROM memories, plainto_tsquery('english', $1) query
WHERE workspace_id = $2 AND deleted_at IS NULL AND tsv @@ query
ORDER BY rank DESC LIMIT $3
```
3. The `memories` table already has a `tsv` tsvector column (verified in schema) — use it directly.
4. Keep the `wal_events` path for other source types (spec, story, archive) that don't have their own tables.
acceptanceCriteria: Keyword search for memory source type queries the memories table instead of wal_events
Uses the existing tsv tsvector column on memories table
Filters by workspace_id and deleted_at IS NULL
Other source types (spec, story, archive) still use their existing search paths
hybridSearch() returns memory results from the memories table
npx tsc --noEmit passes in backend/

userStories.title: Add Memory Count to Context Injection Summary
userStories.description:
The context injection summary card shows `Memory: 0 entries` because `buildCatalogContext()` in `specs.ts` counts memory entries from `MEMORY.md` filesystem file (regex matching `## YYYY-MM-DD` headings). The actual memories are in the `memories` DB table (139 entries).

Update the memory count in the context summary:
1. In `backend/src/routes/specs.ts`, after `buildCatalogContext()` (around line ~776), query the memories table for a count: `SELECT COUNT(*) as cnt FROM memories WHERE workspace_id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL`.
2. Use this DB count instead of (or in addition to) the regex-based `memoryEntryCount` from MEMORY.md.
3. Update `precomputedContextSummary.memoryEntries` to use the higher of the two counts (DB count or filesystem count).
4. This ensures the UI shows the actual number of available memories, not just what's in the filesystem MEMORY.md.
acceptanceCriteria: Memory count in context summary reflects memories table count (not just MEMORY.md regex)
Query uses workspace_id filter and excludes deleted memories
Shows the higher of DB count and filesystem count
Context injection card shows '139 entries' (or actual count) instead of '0 entries'
npx tsc --noEmit passes in backend/
